title: Ice Lake (microprocessor)
text:
Ice Lake was designed by Intel Israel's processor design team in Haifa, Israel.[1,2]

Ice Lake is built on the Sunny Cove microarchitecture.[3,4] Intel released details of Ice Lake during Intel Architecture Day in December 2018, stating that the Sunny Cove core Ice Lake would be focusing on single-thread performance, new instructions, and scalability improvements. Intel stated that the performance improvements would be achieved by making the core "deeper, wider, and smarter".[4]

Ice Lake features Intel's Gen11 graphics, increasing the number of execution units to 64, from 24 or 48 in Gen9.5 graphics, achieving over 1 TFLOPS of compute performance. Each execution unit supports 7 threads, meaning that the design has 512 concurrent pipelines. Feeding these execution units is a 3 megabyte L3 cache, a four-fold increase from Gen9.5, alongside the increased memory bandwidth enabled by LPDDR4X on low-power mobile platforms.Gen11 graphics introduces tile-based rendering. It also features Coarse Pixel Shading (CPS), which is Intel's implementation of variable-rate shading (VRS). The architecture also includes an all-new HEVC encoder design.[4] On August 1, 2019, Intel released the specifications of Ice Lake -U and -Y CPUs.[5] The Y-series CPUs lost their -Y suffix and m3 naming. Instead, Intel uses a trailing number before the GPU type to indicate their package power; "0" corresponds to 9W, "5" to 15W, and "8" to 28W. Furthermore, the first two numbers in the model number correspond to the generation of the chip, while the third number dictates the family the CPU belongs to (i3, i5, etc.); thus, a 1035G7 would be a 10th generation Core i5 with a package power of 15 watts and a G7 GPU.

Pre-orders for laptops featuring Ice Lake CPUs started in August 2019, followed by shipments in September.[6]

### CPU

Intel Sunny Cove CPU cores[7]

On average 18% increase in IPC in comparison to 2015 Skylake running at the same frequency and memory configuration[8,9]

Dynamic Tuning 2.0 which allows the CPU to stay at turbo frequencies for longer[10,11]

TAGE-like directional branch predictor (with a global history size of 194 taken branches)[12]

Hardware acceleration for SHA operations (Secure Hash Algorithms)

Intel Deep Learning Boost, used for machine learning/artificial intelligence inference acceleration[13,11]

PCI Express 4.0 on Ice Lake-SP

### GPU

Gen 11 GPU with up to 64 execution units (From 24 and 48 EU)[14,15]

4K at 120 Hz, 5K, 8K display output[16]

Variable Rate Shading[11,17]

DisplayPort 1.4a with Display Stream Compression; HDMI 2.0b

Up to 1.15 TFLOPS of computational performance

Two HEVC 10-bit encode pipelines, either two 4K 60Hz RGB/ 4:4:4 streams simultaneously or one 8K 30Hz 4:2:2[11]

VP9 8-bit and 10-bit hardware encoding for all supported platforms as part of Intel Quick Sync Video[18,19,20]

Integer and nearest neighbor image scaling[21,22]

4th Gen IPU[23]

### Package

10 nm transistors[24] (originally called 10 nm+ transistors in older naming scheme)[25]

New memory controller with DDR4 3200 and LPDDR4X 3733 support

Integrated support for Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax)

Thunderbolt 3 support[26]
